fields.title: قصر ابراہیم
fields.summary: مٹی کی دیواروں اور کھجور کے تنوں کی چھتوں والا قلعہ، جس کے اندر مسجد، سپاہیوں کی رہائش گاہیں اور برج یکجا ہیں۔
fields.body: ہفوف کے قلب میں قصر ابراہیم (یعنی ابراہیم کا محل) صدیوں کی تبدیلیوں کا گواہ بنا کھڑا ہے۔ یہ عیش و عشرت کا محل نہیں بلکہ ایک قلعہ ہے، جس کی ایک ہی فصیل کے اندر وہ کچھ اکٹھا ہے جو کم ہی یکجا ہوتا ہے: نفیس گنبد والی مسجد، سپاہیوں کی رہائش گاہیں، نگرانی کے برج، اصطبل اور گودام۔ اسے خلیجی خطے کے روایتی انداز میں تعمیر کیا گیا: دیواریں بھوسا ملی مٹی کی ہیں۔ چھتیں کھجور کے تنوں، شندل نامی لکڑی (جو کبھی خلیجی خطے میں درآمد کی جاتی تھی) اور پتھر کی ہیں۔ مینار کے اوپر تک پتھر کی چکر دار سیڑھیاں جاتی ہیں۔ اگر آپ اس کے کشادہ صحن میں گھومیں اور دیکھیں کہ گنبد محراب پر کیسے سایہ کیے ہوئے ہے، تو تاریخ کی وہ تہیں پڑھ لیں گے جو نسل در نسل جمتی چلی گئیں۔ آج یہ قلعہ الاحساء کے ورثے کے نمایاں ترین مقامات میں سے ایک ہے، اور ان عمارتوں میں شامل ہے جن کی بنا پر 2018 میں الاحساء کے نخلستان کو یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست میں جگہ ملی۔
fields.bestTime: دن میں، تاکہ آپ طرز تعمیر کی باریکیاں اور اندرونی صحن کی روشنی دیکھ سکیں

fields.summary: اسلام کی قدیم ترین مساجد میں سے ایک، اور مدینہ منورہ کے بعد پہلی جگہ جہاں جمعہ کی نماز ادا کی گئی۔
fields.body: مسجد جواثا کو وہ مرتبہ حاصل ہے جس کی برابری کم ہی مقامات کر سکتے ہیں۔ یہ اسلام کی قدیم ترین مساجد میں سے ایک ہے، اور کہا جاتا ہے کہ مدینہ منورہ کی مسجد نبوی کے بعد یہ پہلی جگہ ہے جہاں جمعہ کی نماز ادا کی گئی۔ بتایا جاتا ہے کہ یہ نماز قبیلہ بنو عبد القیس کے لوگوں نے ادا کی، جو اس سرزمین پر آباد تھے۔ مٹی کی اس سادہ سی عمارت کا جو حصہ باقی ہے، وہ اپنی جسامت سے زیادہ باوقار ہے۔ اس کی محرابوں اور دیواروں کے سامنے کھڑے ہوں تو نماز اور اجتماع کی وہ صدیاں آنکھوں کے سامنے آ جاتی ہیں جو الاحساء کے نخلستان میں گزریں۔ اس نخلستان کے لوگ سب سے پہلے اسلام قبول کرنے والوں میں سے تھے۔ اس مسجد کی مرمت “شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبے” کے تحت ہوئی۔ یہ تاریخی مساجد کے لیے ایک ترقیاتی منصوبہ ہے، اور اسی کے تحت الاحساء کی مسجد الجعلانیہ، مسجد شیخ محمد بن ابی بکر الملا اور مسجد الحبیش کی بھی مرمت ہوئی۔ مسجد جواثا کی زیارت کسی عمارت کو دیکھنے سے بڑھ کر وقت کا سفر ہے، ایک ایسا لمحہ جو آپ کو اس جگہ کی تاریخ کی ایک گہری جڑ سے جوڑ دیتا ہے۔

fields.title: قصر صاہود
fields.summary: المبرز کے قلب میں سات برجوں والا ایک بہت بڑا دفاعی قلعہ، جو یونیسکو کی فہرست میں شامل الاحساء کے نخلستان کا ایک حصہ ہے۔
fields.body: المبرز کے قلب میں قصر صاہود کھڑا ہے۔ یہ تقریباً 10,000 مربع میٹر پر پھیلا ایک بہت بڑا قلعہ ہے۔ نگرانی کے سات برج اس کی چھ میٹر اونچی فصیلوں کی حفاظت کرتے ہیں، اور کبھی اس کے گرد ایک دفاعی خندق ہوا کرتی تھی۔ یہ بارہویں صدی ہجری کے اواخر میں تعمیر ہوا۔ الاحساء نے علی پاشا کی لشکر کشی کے خلاف جو مزاحمت کی، یہ قلعہ اس کے واقعات کا گواہ ہے۔ اس کی فصیلوں کے اندر ایک مسجد، ایک کنواں، گودام، سپاہیوں کے کمرے اور اصطبل تھے، اور محاصرے کے دنوں میں شہر کے لوگ یہیں پناہ لیتے تھے۔ ورثہ کمیشن نے اس کی مرمت کی۔ الاحساء کا نخلستان 2018 میں یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست میں درج ہوا، اور آج یہ قلعہ اس کے بارہ حصوں میں سے ایک ہے۔

accuracy.why: 'Al-Ahsa's first formal government school', flat, in an apposition as the source has it, the noun not widened; 1937 in the summary, both calendars in the body; the four places of the location all there. Two points off: «شروع ہوا» is the Arabic's verb where the English says 'opened' (ruling P23); the name carries a gloss the source does not write («(یعنی امیریہ اسکول)»); 'stands on the rise' is «جس ٹیلے پر یہ بنا ہے اسے ام الخبیصی کہتے ہیں»; and 'the region's sons' is «اس علاقے کے بچے».

nativeness.why: No string of this page changes in round 3. The third reader calls the paragraph 'plain, clear Urdu and the easiest reading of the five pages'; «اسکول» passed him in all four places, the gloss 'earns its place', and «بچے» is in a sentence he quotes as plain. Three points off: the opening sentence holds four pieces before its verb ('I was holding my breath'; his remedy is round 1's «… ہے», which two readers took for a school of today, so the apposition stays); «تعلیمی بیداری» says little to two readers; «نامی بازار» beside «نامی مقام» is stiff to the second and 'just a place called' to the third; «ثقافت کا گھر» in the summary reads as a figure of speech to all three; and «شروع ہوا» is a class's verb to the third where the second passed it.

compliance.why: «“بیت الثقافہ” (ثقافت کا گھر) نامی مقام» as rulings P3b and P15 build it; the year pairs; the hours cell with «اتوار تا جمعرات» and « · »; the loan spelled as its entry; the gloss straight after the page's own name. Two points off: four names of nine leaves are pending, the page's own title among them («مدرسہ امیریہ», «ام الخبیصی», «النعاثل», «بیت الثقافہ»).

fit.why: The card was enough for all three readers to plan with, and the common noun is the word they use. One point off: the title says 'seminary' to two readers until the summary and the gloss put it right, and the gloss cannot say what «امیریہ» means. What the building holds today is the source's silence.

fields.title: مدرسہ امیریہ
fields.summary: الاحساء کا پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری اسکول، جو 1937 میں شروع ہوا۔ اس کی تاریخی عمارت آج ثقافت کا گھر ہے۔
fields.body: مدرسہ امیریہ (یعنی امیریہ اسکول)، الاحساء کا پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری اسکول، پرانے ہفوف کے مشرق میں، محلہ النعاثل میں واقع ہے۔ جس ٹیلے پر یہ بنا ہے اسے ام الخبیصی کہتے ہیں، اور سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار یہاں سے قریب ہے۔ اسکول میں پڑھائی 1356 ہجری (1937 عیسوی) میں کرائے کی ایک عمارت میں شروع ہوئی، اور اس کی مستقل عمارت 1360 ہجری (1941 عیسوی) میں کھلی۔ یہ عمارت عرب اسلامی طرز تعمیر میں بنی ہے: دروازہ محراب دار ہے اور اندرونی صحن کے گرد برآمدے ہیں۔ اس علاقے کے بچے نسل در نسل یہیں پڑھتے رہے۔ مرمت کے بعد یہ عمارت اب “بیت الثقافہ” (ثقافت کا گھر) نامی مقام ہے، جو الاحساء کی تعلیمی بیداری کی یاد کو محفوظ رکھتا ہے۔

blind_reader_rulings.reason: Not a leaf of this batch: «یہ مقام محفوظ کریں» is the interface string fav.add, locked with batch b0-ui. The heading is trails.partOf and the path label is the breadcrumb's, both interface strings of b0-ui; 'Trails' reads as roads in the English too, logged there. His wording («سیر کے ان منصوبوں میں شامل») and his remark that one word does two jobs are carried to the interface with the two earlier readers'.

Carried to it: «سیر مکمل کر سکتے ہیں» has now been heard as translated by every reader of the two attraction batches whose remark on it is on record here (five), and this reader's remedy is word for word the first reader's («… جو آپ اسی سیر میں دیکھ سکتے ہیں»).

The interface string det.nearby.note (b0-ui), not a leaf of this batch; he understood it on the second read. Carried to the interface: the first reader had faulted the qualifier that trails after the verb, and this one adds that the line does not say the practical point, that the drive is longer than the straight line.

The cards change shape because the five sources carry different rows (hours and fee as two rows, as one, as a park's, or none; a best time and a duration on some pages only; an FAQ on three), and the area line opens with «الاحساء،» only where its source names Al-Ahsa as the larger place (ruling P20; the three other lines are the open item N30). An artifact of the plain-text page, for the third reader in a row: the block is the home-page featured card, whose kicker is never rendered on the detail page; the tool prints it after the back button. It is not a second label of the page. His remark on the kicker «نایاب ورثہ» ('what one says of something that cannot be found') is one reader's on a word whose common sense is 'rare'; the second reader called the same kicker vague; the field's only source is the Arabic «إرثٌ نادر», and no count separates the word from its neighbour («نایاب ورثہ» and «نادر ورثہ» stand on no reference page). Kept, on record for the home-page card when it is next read in place.

Rulings P17 and P1, not reopened: no vowel mark and no pronunciation gloss is written on a name (the build guard rejects the kasra), and «ہفوف» is the one name with a settled Urdu form without the article. That no page says what Hofuf and Al-Mubarraz are is the source's silence (SD10 of the calibration). The remark has now been made by all three readers of this batch and by b2's; it is on record for whoever may reopen P17.

One reader of three on a word the other two read on three pages without a remark, and the word the reference site uses more often of exactly these things, counted in this round: «مسجد کی مرمت» 67 pages against «مسجد کی بحالی» 20, «قلعے کی مرمت» 13 against 4, «عمارت کی مرمت» 24 against 5. The heading «سیاحوں کے لیے معلومات» is the interface's (det.visitInfo, b0-ui, ruling P27) and is not a leaf of this batch; the row's «زائرین» is item N17, and he says himself that for a mosque it 'is the right word'. Carried to the interface: the heading jars on a mosque page for two of this batch's three readers and for the readers of the sister batch.

The template prints the number of the World Heritage component bare after the badge, in every language; like both earlier readers he took 1563 for a year. Logged by b0-ui; nothing in the page fields can label it.

Who Ibrahim was, who built the fort and when are in neither source, and 'stands witness to centuries of change' is the source's sentence in both languages. Like the second reader, he thinks first of the Prophet Ibrahim. What the Urdu owns passed him: the gloss with the sentence that answers it 'is a good touch and reads well'.

'What rarely meets' is the site's own claim, the sister page lists nearly the same contents, and 'rarely' opens the praise of three pages because their sources do. Three readers have now heard the mould; the wording of round 1 is quoted without a fault on its make.

Three readers of three, in two wordings, have taken «شندل» for a misprint of the word for sandalwood. The name is the Arabic's, built by the transliteration rule (entry pending), and the bracket is the owner's ruled explanation (build check C40: 'timber once imported to the Gulf'), which says neither which wood nor from where. Round 2's «نامی لکڑی» tells him it is a wood and cannot tell him which; no wording can without a fact no source gives, and a vowel mark is barred (ruling P17). «خلیجی خطے» twice in two sentences is the sources' 'Gulf' twice, and the bare form of round 1 read as odd to the second reader. Kept; raised to the owner as the one thing on this page that only a fact can mend.

The picture and the promise are the source's, image for image ('watch the dome shade the mihrab, and you will read layers of history accumulated generation by generation'), and the English drops what the Arabic has ('in its walls'). All three readers stopped here. What round 2 repaired passed him: the condition is said first and he did not read an invitation. His remedy for the second half replaces the source's figure with another statement and is not taken (rulings P24, P25); it goes to the owner with the sentence.

First point applied, with proof finding 2 (changes 0 and 1): «شہر کی» is gone from the body and from the answer, so no unnamed city stands in the World Heritage claim. Second point kept: «قلب» in the bodies and «وسط» in the cards are two source wordings ('in the heart of', «في قلب»; 'Central', «وسط»), each with one Urdu word; two readers have noticed the switch and both call the words fine. As round 1 ruled on the first reader's same remark: the blues are the places where the sources say 'blue', and the best-time row is the source's sentence; cutting it to its first clause would trade the content of the field for a plainer register (ruling P24). Two readers of three now; the option for the owner stays on record («غروب آفتاب سے ذرا پہلے»).

Remains that 'still guard the place' are the source's figure in both languages, and whether the buildings stand or can be entered is in neither; his remedy drops the figure and is not taken (ruling P24). The chain in the last answer («پرانی بندرگاہ کی مٹی کی عمارتوں کے آثار») was read by the two earlier readers without a remark; one reader, kept and charged.
Applied in his own words: «چل پھر سکتے ہیں» and «جہاں سے». The bare verb of round 2 was the judge's; no road is named, so the shift the first proof pass found does not come back.

A label that says hours over a value with none, and an 'open public site' that does not say whether one may come at any hour or enter the fort: as open in both sources. Said by all three readers. «کھلا» is as wide as the source's 'open'; that it can also be heard as open-air is charged under fit.

'East of Al-Ahsa' with no distance or drive, whether one may swim, and anything on shade, washrooms or food are in no source of the page. Nothing is supplied, as he asks ('missing, not for me to guess').

CONFIRMED from the pack, by a third reader with the same grade: 'what remains', 'was restored' and 'open to visitors' stand side by side in the sources; the only hours on the card are a park's; whether prayers are held and when the mosque itself may be entered is the owner's unanswered question. No visiting time and no status is written.

The park stands in the card and the FAQ and nowhere in the body, in both languages; what it is, whether the mosque stands inside it and what decides 10 as against 15 riyals are in no source. That all three readers ask what kind of place a «تفریح گاہ» is, is recorded with the term (the Arabic's word is as wide) and charged under fit.

The worst defect of the batch, seen by all three readers: the summary flat and 'after Medina', the body and the answer hedged and 'after the Prophet's Mosque', in both languages. Each field keeps its source's strength; the Urdu levels nothing.

Applied in his own sentence, in the body and in faq[2].a (changes 3 and 8): the reporting verb first. It is the wording the proof pass had put on record should a reader take the second parse, and it keeps what rounds 1 and 2 required of the clause: the guarded sentence untouched and closed at its own stop, the tribe under a hedge of its own.

Applied in his own sentence, less one word: three pointing words become one, «حجم» gives way to his «جسامت», and the opening no longer hangs on the sentence about the tribe. «کہیں» is not taken: it is the degree word stage 4 removed under the fence. calibration.question: The gloss for a name whose Arabic generic is opaque or a false friend in Urdu («عین», «سوق», «قصر», and since round 2 «مدرسہ»), in running text: its form, and where it is owed.
candidates: A — the named gloss «(یعنی … کا …)» at the first body mention of every such name, passing mentions included (the text of stages 1 to 5)
B — the same form, owed only on the page whose own name it is; a passing mention stands bare

calibration.question: The opening of a fort page whose English says 'stands X, a … fort' or 'X rises …: a … fortress': what follows the verb of place, and the verb.
candidates: A — «X … کھڑا ہے: … ایک … قلعہ۔» (stages 1 to 5 of both batches; sahood until round 2)
B — «X … واقع ہے۔ یہ … قلعہ ہے …» (b2 since its round 1)
C — the sentence of place with the page's own verb, then a sentence with its verb for what the building is (sahood, round 3)
calibration.evidence: b2's item. Ruled B in b2's round 1 for its three fort pages, on its first reader: after the colon came 'a piece with no verb', and '«کھڑا ہے» for a building's location is the English stands; «واقع ہے» is what Urdu writes'; b2's second reader wrote «واقع ہے» himself in both sentences he rewrote. Reference (b2): «قلعہ واقع ہے» 10 pages, «قلعہ کھڑا ہے» 1. b1's sahood: the first reader read «… المبرز کے قلب میں کھڑا ہے: …» without a remark on verb or colon; the second wrote the opening himself, the place first, with «کھڑا ہے»; the third read it so and faulted one thing: 'the colon followed by a clause with no verb is an English habit' (42, minor). On qasr-ibrahim «… صدیوں کی تبدیلیوں کا گواہ بنا کھڑا ہے» was read by all three without a remark on the verb. The proof passes (b1 on its round 2, finding 8; b2 on its round 2): the twin pages were ruled two ways in one round, and the words of round 1's N31 carried no limit.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: One wording for both batches. (1) What the building is does not hang verbless after a colon: it has a sentence of its own with its verb, after the sentence that says where the building is. This is b2's ruling, adopted for sahood in round 3 on its third reader: «المبرز کے قلب میں قصر صاہود کھڑا ہے۔ یہ تقریباً 10,000 مربع میٹر پر پھیلا ایک بہت بڑا قلعہ ہے۔» (2) The verb of place: «واقع ہے» on b2's three pages (muhairis, khuzam, uqair-castle), whose sources say 'stands' and whose two readers chose it; «کھڑا ہے» on sahood, whose English says 'rises', whose second reader wrote that verb for this very sentence and whose three readers passed it. Neither verb is barred by this ruling outside the pages named: the sentence of b2's round 1 that «کھڑا ہے» is not written for a location holds for b2's three pages and is not a rule for every fort page. THE DIFFERENCE in (2) is kept and recorded by both judges; one verb for every fort page is for the judge of the next fort page, with a reader before him. «… گواہ بنا کھڑا ہے» on qasr-ibrahim is the source's image of a witness and no statement of place.
calibration.binds: b1: sahood body (its first two sentences). LEFT TO b2: its three openings stand as they are («… واقع ہے۔ یہ … قلعہ ہے …»); nothing moves, and its judge can take this wording over or keep its own with the same limit.
calibration.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on a fort page no colon follows the opening verb of place, and what the building is has its own verb.

On qasr-ibrahim all three ask how a dome shades a niche seen from a courtyard, and the first and the third add that the word may mean an arch there ('or is «محراب» here an arch?') — the source's picture. b2 (read for this word only): its second reader took «محراب دار چھتیں» on jabri-mosque for the prayer niche, its judge wrote «قوس نما چھتیں», and its third reader calls that 'a geometry-book word; for a building I expect «محراب دار»'.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: A, for b1's three places, which stand as three readers read them: the architectural arch is «محراب» (oblique plural «محرابوں»; 'arched' is «محراب دار»), and the niche is «محراب» in the singular, in a sentence that names the mosque or its dome. No other word is brought in for the arch: it is the dictionary's word, the word a reader of b2 expects for a building, and the only doubt the plural raised on a mosque page was answered by the plural. Where the word stands beside a mosque's roof or vault and can be taken for the niche, the judge of that page chooses; this ruling neither bars b2's describing word nor asks for it.
calibration.binds: b1: jawatha-mosque body, ameeriah body, qasr-ibrahim body (all unchanged). LEFT TO b2: the vaults of jabri-mosque — its round 2's describing word, or back to «محراب دار» as its third reader expects — are b2's to rule in its last round; either is within this ruling, and in both the vault is described, not named.
calibration.guard: None mechanical. For the proofreader: on a mosque page the arch is marked by the plural or by the suffix of «محراب دار».
